overview.description: Escoba (Spanish for 'Broom') is the Spanish variant of Scopa, a fishing-capture game. The defining mechanic: a player captures ALL cards from the table by playing a card that, combined with the table cards, sums to exactly 15. This 'sweep' (escoba) earns bonus points. Card values: A=1, 2-7=face value, J=8, Q=9, K=10. Targets: Most cards, Most Coins, 7 of Coins (Siete Bello), and sweeps.

history.origins: Escoba is the Spanish adaptation of the Italian game Scopa. 'Escoba de 15' means 'Broom of 15'â€”sweeping the table clean. It is particularly popular in Argentina, Spain, and the Spanish-speaking Caribbean.
timeline: 1800s: Scopa spreads from Italy to Spain as Escoba.
Present: Standard card game in Spain and Latin America, especially Argentina.
history.evolution: While Scopa uses a target sum of 15 in Italian regions, Escoba makes the '15 sum' the ONLY valid capture condition (where Scopa allows pairing by rank too). This simplification makes Escoba easier to learn but equally scoring-rich.
history.cultural: A popular trattoria and cafÃ© game across Argentina, Uruguay, and Spain. Often paired with other Spanish games in home settings.

setup.deck: 40-card Spanish baraja (A, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, J, Q, K in 4 suits: Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs). Values: A=1, 2-7=face, J=8, Q=9, K=10.
setup.dealing: 3 cards each; 4 cards face-up on table. Redeal 3 when hands empty until deck done.

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to score 21 or more points by capturing cards that sum to exactly 15, collecting majority points in multiple categories, and earning bonus points for sweeps.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing one card to capture table cards that sum to exactly 15 with the played card. Captured cards and the playing card are taken and stored face-down. If no capture is possible, the card remains face-up on the table. Players cycle through their dealt cards, and new cards are dealt after all players have played their three cards. Play continues until the deck is exhausted.
keyRules: Only after a complete table clear is an Escoba scored.
Setenta (optional): Each player/team selects the highest card per suit summing to a maximum = best Setenta wins 1pt.

strategy.basic: Always execute an Escoba if possibleâ€”it's 1 guaranteed point AND clears the table. Seven of Coins (Siete Bello) is worth 1 point just for capturing itâ€”prioritize.
strategy.intermediate: Table Control: Don't leave a 15-sum combination on the table for the opponentâ€”add a 'blocking' card of the wrong value to break their potential sweep.
strategy.advanced: Coins Tracking: In 4-player teams, track the count of Coins captured. Most Coins = 11 or more out of 20. Setenta (if used): Q (9pts in Coins) + 7 of other suits typically scores highest.
tips: Save the 7 of Coins (Siete Bello) as it's worth 1 point just for existing in your capture pile.

edgeCases.text: If the four face-up table cards sum to exactly 15, the dealer captures them before any play and scores one escoba; if they sum to 30, the dealer scores two escobas and the player to dealer's right leads to an empty table.
When the deck is exhausted and all hands are played, any cards left on the table go to the last player or team that made a capture; this does not count as an escoba.

If the played card cannot form a sum of 15 with any set of table cards, the card is left face-up on the table (trail); capture is not mandatory when possible but if a capture is made the cards must be taken.

engine.deckDescription: Standard 40-card Spanish baraja: forty cards in four Spanish suits (Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs), with ranks Ace, 2 through 7, Jack, Queen, and King; eights and nines are omitted and no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: Spanish suit set: four suits—Oros (Coins), Copas (Cups), Espadas (Swords), and Bastos (Clubs)—each with ten cards; point values in Escoba are A=1, 2-7=face, J=8, Q=9, K=10.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped forty rank set for Spanish baraja: Ace (1), 2 through 7 (face value), Jack (8), Queen (9), King (10); eights and nines removed; ten cards per suit for capture and fifteen-point scoring.
